A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same AudioX paper with 26 readable pages, including the complete appendix. Text extraction, rendered-page comparison, and PDF-object inspection establish identical manuscript content; differences are confined to the arXiv stamp/link and embedded metadata.

before.justification: v3 reports original AudioX benchmark and ablation results in Tables 1–4, additional generation experiments in Tables A.4–A.6, and a human evaluation in Figure A.2.

after.justification: v4 retains the original AudioX benchmark experiments, ablations, supplementary generation results, and human evaluation in the same tables and figures.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the identical diffusion-transformer architecture, Multimodal Adaptive Fusion module, modality handling, diffusion process, and training objective.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation coverage is identical, including the datasets in Table A.1, instruction-following benchmarks, and appendix experiments on inpainting, music completion, and zero-shot image-to-audio generation.

E2.justification: Comparator membership within each experiment is unchanged, including Tables 1–2, A.4 and A.6 and the user-study comparisons in Figure A.2.

E3.justification: Model configurations, training budgets, data splits, sample counts, preprocessing, metrics, automated judging, and human-evaluation procedures are identical in Section 5 and Appendices A.1–A.4.

E4.justification: The data-curation and MAF-component ablations in Tables 3–4, modality analyses in Figure A.3, out-of-domain evaluation, and qualitative cases in Figures A.4–A.5 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical: tables retain point estimates and Figure A.2 retains mean human ratings. Neither version provides additional repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries, plotted results, rankings, and qualitative findings match across the main text and appendix, including Tables 1–4 and A.4–A.6 and Figures A.2–A.5.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4 and the formal evaluation definitions in Appendix A.3 are identical. No assumptions, derivations, propositions, or proofs are added, removed, or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about unified multimodal generation, IF-caps, adaptive fusion, cross-modal regularization, and instruction-following performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations of data quality, fusion mechanisms, generalization, and multimodal conditioning are unchanged in Sections 5.3–5.5 and Appendix A.4. No limitations or applicability qualifications are added or removed.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, compute requirements, annotation procedures, and evaluation instructions are identical. Code, dataset, and benchmark availability statements and access links are also unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, citations throughout the manuscript, and the reference list are identical. Positioning relative to specialist generators, existing datasets, and diffusion models remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The page-1 arXiv stamp changes from v3, 14 Feb 2026 to v4, 15 Apr 2026. Embedded author metadata adds Liumeng Xue, already present in both printed author lists. Manuscript wording and structure are identical.

P2.justification: All figures, tables, captions, axes, legends, and placements are identical. Rendered manuscript bodies match on every page; the updated margin stamp introduces no substantive layout change.

improvement.justification: The complete main text and appendix retain identical methods, evidence, explanations, and visual presentation. Correcting embedded author metadata improves metadata accuracy, but the printed attribution already matched; this and the version-stamp update produce no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
